entry.title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
entry.summary:
We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: The Covering Radius of $\text{RM}(1,9)$ is Precisely $242$
entry.summary:
Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Muller code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius, so that $\rho(1,n)$ is the largest possible nonlinearity of a Boolean function in $n$ variables. For odd $n$, the value of $\rho(1,n)$ was previously known only for $n\le 7$. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, but the exact determination of $\rho(1,9)$ has been a long-standing open question.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Birthday Estimators Are Uniformly Optimal for Renyi Entropy
entry.summary:
Collisions are a basic probe of unknown distributions, used for testing and for counting substructures in graphs, and they underlie Rényi entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty with applications in cryptography, machine learning, physics, and biology. Motivated by this, we study the natural birthday estimator. We prove Bernstein-type concentration for it and show that it is minimax optimal, uniformly and jointly in alphabet size, order, accuracy, and confidence, with no sample splitting, clipping, or median aggregation.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #algorithms #probability-stats

entry.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption for Small Batches of Complex Numbers. We propose a new approximate homomorphic encryption scheme to process small batches of complex numbers.
entry.summary:
We propose a new approximate homomorphic encryption scheme to process small batches of complex numbers. Leveled operations are based on a new shaped rounding, whose error is a multiple of a fixed public ring element $g$, small on the data slots and larger on the others. The unused slots form a guard band that is computed on but never decoded, and the polynomial scaling factor $g^{-1}\Delta$ generalizes the CKKS scaling factor, with $g=1$ recovering CKKS.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: ReedWeave: Faster Reed-Solomon Polynomial Commitments from Interleaving and Folding
entry.summary:
Polynomial commitment schemes (PCSs) allow a prover to commit to a polynomial and later prove its evaluations succinctly. Among hash-based constructions, FRI (Ben-Sasson et al., ICALP 2018) and its follow-up works achieve polylogarithmic proofs by recursively ``folding'' Reed-Solomon (RS) codes. However, their concrete evaluation costs remain relatively high, as the first few folding rounds operate on the largest codewords and dominate the prover work.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust

entry.title: Efficient and Compact High-order Masking Raccoon on Memory Constrained Devices
entry.summary:
Raccoon, presented at CRYPTO 2024, is a provably secure lattice-based signature scheme featuring an $O(d \log{d})$ masking overhead. Although it did not advance beyond the first-round of NIST's additional call for post-quantum digital signatures, Raccoon remains a promising candidate due to its low masking overhead and strong provable side-channel resistance. This paper proposes the first efficient and compact implementation of high-order Raccoon on the ARM Cortex-M4, with a focus on optimizing its polynomial multiplication, sampling, and memory consumption.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum
